title: Creative director's score of board 3, after Phase 3's rounds 4 and 5 and chapter 15, as the builder's run 8 left it

items.name: Board 3 as built (run 8, 18:19 UTC, on version 13)

reasons.craft: Panels 2 to 4 compose 13 forms, round 5 and 25 rules at true size on both grounds, with grayscale and tables in folds, and each panel 1 item sets its pictures straight under its recommendation. Four one-approval items set whole plates or page strips where the change is a few lines: "Where to start" at 19,547 px, Rule 14.144's pips at 14,796, Rules 14.1 to 14.14 at 11,379 and S40 at 6,792 for five date cells. That leaves panel 1 at 144,509 px at 1440 (B3-M4, B3-S1).
reasons.clarity: The reply list, answer-first items, plain words where codes stood and terms defined at first use let Dustin say what each item asks from its first lines. The second pass score table never says what its small figures are or that all 14 items are now ready (B3-S4).
reasons.brand_fidelity: The board's chrome uses eight token colors with no Pillar Red or Prussian. With the wordmark covered the page reads as Oath & Action by Newsprint, Inter Tight and the evidence chips. Every recommendation keeps a settled element or offers its change as a named reply. Reply 10 as worded would shrink the wordmark on 375 px phones that need no change (B3-M2).
reasons.usefulness: Dustin can act on all 24 replies in about three minutes, with recommendation, reason and picture side by side, and every link resolves (48 on the page, 63 to the chapters page). The "Where to start" pair cannot show the change it asks him to approve (B3-M4).
reasons.evidence_honesty: The keyline item calls 2.96 to 1 "under the 3 to 1 that … WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11 ask of a mark a reader needs" without saying whether the plates fail AA, since they also name their targets in words, and it omits the grayscale cost (B3-M1). The masthead item says the menu drops at 360 to 375 px, where its own 375 px picture shows one line (B3-M2). Panel 1 prints the page at 12,178,927 bytes and a 459,192 mean where panels 5 and 8 print version 13's 12,178,909 and the report's 459,191 (B3-M3). S59's sketch prints a label the item does not mention (B3-S2).
reasons.accessibility: The wrapped copy passes the board check at 1440, 390 and 360 px: no type under 13 px, no low contrast, no sideways scroll and 40 focus stops with rings. Every picture has alt, size and lazy loading, and tables are live text. Panel 1's alts name the item and the build, not what the picture shows (B3-S5).

items.to_ready: Land B3-M1 to B3-M4: evidence honesty reaches 4 with M1 to M3; M4 makes the one picture pair that cannot show its change show it. No score sits under 3.

verdict:
Board 3 meets board 2's bar for how Dustin decides. Panel 1 opens with the 24 numbered replies, each with its recommendation and a link, then the reply line; the cover says the replies take three minutes and the whole panel 39, which is true. Every item opens with its answer and recommendation, the named alternatives are one phrase each ("Chapter 02 too", "Keyline everywhere", "Run the search"), and no decision code or file name sits on the face. Panels 2 to 4 set round 4's forms, round 5 and all of chapter 15 at true size in board 2's anatomy, and the scores panel matches my files cell for cell.

Four things keep it from shipping, all small. The keyline item states its contrast cost without saying whether the recommended state still meets WCAG 2.2 AA, and leaves out the grayscale cost its own plates show. The masthead item recommends the smaller wordmark up to 375 px, where its own picture shows the larger one already fits. Panel 1 prints a page size from an earlier build. The "Where to start" pair cannot show its change.

Read against the brief's settled list, no recommendation changes a settled element outright. Reply 11 keeps the atlas visual system's target. Reply 7 keeps chapter 02. Reply 4 keeps the coverage plan's questions. Reply 16 touches System 1's read-aloud device without naming it (B3-S3); in my reading, as the owner of DR-36's finishing list, it keeps that device and its rule. Each recommendation reads the same from the left and the right. Reply 18 swaps no law to even the sides, and the sixteen example lines name no party.

B3-M1.title: The keyline item leaves its accessibility cost unruled and its grayscale cost unstated.
B3-M1.what: The recommendation says the ring "stays at 2.96 to 1 on all five plates, under the 3 to 1 that Rule 05.5 and the web accessibility standard (WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11) ask of a mark a reader needs". If that is a WCAG failure, "As recommended" approves an AA failure on five plates, and Master Brief section 22 asks for AA. If it is not one, because each plate also names its targets in words ("It acts where the marks turn red", "Its targets, from the atlas"), the sentence overstates the cost. Read by luma, Rule 15.11 today turns its two targeted pills a mid gray, lighter than the untargeted pill's black outline, so in a one-ink copy the target reads weakest. With the keyline it reads strongest. The board shows color only.
B3-M1.fix: Put the accessibility lead's ruling in one sentence: whether the five plates meet WCAG 2.2 AA without the keyline, and why. Add the grayscale cost in one sentence, with Rule 15.11 today and with the keyline as a grayscale pair. Keep the recommendation as D3-2284 set it.
B3-M1.owner: Editor (words), from the accessibility lead's ruling through the main session; builder (the grayscale pair, by the page's own filter or a luma conversion, labeled as which).

B3-M2.title: The masthead item recommends the smaller wordmark where the larger one fits.
B3-M2.what: The item's own "What changed" measures the fault at 360 to 372 px, and the register names "the masthead at 360 to 372 px". Its picture "Today at 375 px" shows the 24 px master and the menu button on one line, 90 px tall. The recommendation "use the 16 px wordmark up to 375 px" would swap in the 16 px master on 373 to 375 px phones, 375 being the commonest phone width, where nothing needs fixing.
B3-M2.fix: Recommend the switch up to 372 px, so 375 px keeps the 24 px master, and retitle the item "360 to 372 px". If the engineer's measure says the switch cannot land between 372 and 373 px, say what 373 to 375 px loses and offer 375 as the named reply.
B3-M2.owner: Editor (words); data lead (the switch width, from the engineer's measured range); builder (picture labels).

B3-M3.title: Two figures for one page.
B3-M3.where: `#d-Q-PR1` ("Page today 12,178,927 bytes"; "459,192 on average"); panel 5 and panel 8 (12,178,909).
B3-M3.what: The decision file still reads the joined build's report (`build_report`, 12,178,927 bytes). The board's final page is version 13, whose report gives 12,178,909 bytes and a mean of 459,191.
B3-M3.fix: Rerun the counts against version 13's report (`--counts-only`) so every page figure on the board is read from one report.

B3-M4.title: "Where to start" shows two 19,000 px strips that cannot show the change.
B3-M4.where: `#d-where-to-start`, both pictures (288 by 19,087 and 288 by 19,171 px).
B3-M4.what: The item asks approval because the page "no longer scrolls sideways; it used to scroll 33 px". Both pictures are cropped to the 288 px element, so the 33 px overflow is cut off, and the pair first differs 12,158 px down. At 390 px the two stack to about 38,000 px.
B3-M4.fix: Photograph the 320 px window, not the element, around the lines that overflowed, before and after, a few hundred pixels tall each, with the overflow visible in the "before". Drop the whole strips or put them in a fold.

B3-S1.title: Crop three more one-approval items to their change
B3-S1.what_and_fix: Rule 14.144's pips (four whole plates, 14,796 px): one card and the line-up block, before and after. Rules 14.1 to 14.14 (11,379 px): the changed sentences of Rule 14.6. S40 (6,792 px): the five date cells. Whole plates go in the item's fold.

B3-S2.title: S59's sketch does more than its words say
B3-S2.what_and_fix: Lifting 2026's "4.1" also makes 2027's "4.1" print, a label that gave way before, and the lifted label sits about 0.8 points above its point with no leader. The item says "Only the label's place moves." Say what the sketch shows, or set the sketch so only the one label moves.

B3-S3.title: Name the atlas visual system in Reply 16's touches line
B3-S3.what_and_fix: The read-aloud line is System 1's device (`read_aloud()` in its build), and my DR-36 finishing list set "start with more, flip at each minus" beside it. Add DR-36 to "What it touches". Say the new form keeps the device and its rule (it starts with a rise and flips at each minus), and check the key line's "start with more" against the new form. That is my reading as the owner of that list; the main session confirms it in its settled-list read.

B3-S4.title: The second pass score table
B3-S4.what_and_fix: Add one line: "Each cell gives the score after the fix pass, small, then the score after the second pass. With this pass all 14 items are ready."

B3-S5.title: Panel 1's alts say where a picture came from, not what it shows
B3-S5.what_and_fix: Example: "The plate at a 1,440 px window. A picture for "Rule 11.10 …", photographed from version 13 …". Give each the one fact it shows, as panels 2 and 4 do. The "Where to start" alts also nest quotes ("““Where to start” …”").

B3-S6.title: Panel 5's bars carry no 100 percent mark
B3-S6.what_and_fix: so chapter 14's "100.6 percent" bar does not show where its figure falls. Draw the figure's line on each bar.

B3-S7.title: Panel 5's heaviest charts print S96 with no rule
B3-S7.what_and_fix: and its form as the code `columns-moving-average`. Print "14.142" and "Columns with a moving average", as the editor asked.

B3-S8.title: Set my view beside the keyline recommendation
B3-S8.what_and_fix: as board 2 set my view on S12: the text under "My view on the keyline".

B3-S9.title: Panel 6's election data test prints with no full stop
B3-S9.what_and_fix: Use the editor's sentence: "A form keeps election data only where the coverage plan writes its use as an election question."

named_places.1_can_dustin_reply_quickly: Yes. Panel 1's first screen after its intro is the 24 replies (631 words, three minutes) and the reply line. Every reply links to its item, and the three named alternatives are one phrase each.
named_places.2_does_each_item_open_with_its_answer_an: Yes, all 39 items, in that order, then what changed, why, and for held items what it touches and how it keeps what he settled.
named_places.3_settled_elements: No recommendation changes one outright. Reply 16 touches DR-36's read-aloud device without naming it (B3-S3). Reply 10 touches Rule 03.6's two approved masters and names them, but overreaches to 375 px (B3-M2).
named_places.4_left_and_right: Reply 18 recommends the rule the files show and says no law is swapped to even the sides. Of the sixteen example lines, three touch voting (turnout, waiting in line, the mail ballot envelope), each asked as a reader would, with no side named.
named_places.5_numbers_traceable: Every figure I checked reads from a file, except panel 1's page size (B3-M3).

my_view_on_keyline: I would choose "Keyline everywhere". The keyline is a 1 px line inside the ring and a thin edge on the arrowhead. The red, the ring and the pill stay as the atlas draws them. It meets Rule 05.5, which Dustin approved at Gate 2, after DR-36 chose the atlas system. It keeps the target the strongest mark in grayscale and in one-ink copies, where without it the target reads weakest. DR-36 made the atlas system's finishing work the creative director's list, and I would add the keyline to it. The studio's recommendation cannot change a settled element, so this stays my view, and the choice is his.

Read as one reference, every form and rule in the same anatomy at true size.

The keyline choice sets how every red target in the guide reads in grayscale and one-ink print. Today one target has two looks.
At 375 px, the commonest phone width, the masthead shows the larger wordmark today. Reply 10 as worded would change that.
